meta.title: Emerald Champions Complete Battle Guide
meta.ordering: Canonical campaign route; optional fights follow their local chapter; rematches and postgame are separate.
meta.levelRule: Opponent level = active strict cap + authored offset, clamped to levels 1-100.

entries.name: May
entries.plan: The rival always fields the type-counter starter from the same regional trio the player chose. It is level 15, one above the strict cap, with perfect IVs, a Life Orb, its universal Pledge STAB, Return, Toxic, and Protect. The encounter supports all 21 starters across Generations 1-7 through one native counterpart rule, while May and Brendan remain mechanically identical. It introduces Verdant's preparation freedom without pretending the player already owns a full team.
entries.behavior: The normal foe-aware viability AI chooses among offense, Toxic, and Protect. No opening is forced and no hidden lock-and-key sequence is required.
entries.counterplay: There is no single required solution. The player can use any legal coverage or status plan their chosen starter supports, or lean on Focus Sash, Eviolite, Leftovers, Life Orb, or a Choice item from Oldale. Protect, setup, Counter or Mirror Coat, Endeavor, speed control, and direct offense are all viable on different starters.

entries.name: Calvin
entries.theme: Fake Out tempo + Sash Endeavor lure + active speed control
entries.plan: Zorua leads beside Friend Guard Jigglypuff while Illusion makes it appear to be the Mew held in the final slot. Icy Wind and Helping Hand turn the false Mew into immediate pressure; Focus Sash Smeargle then creates a redirection or Fake Out window for the real Mew to use Nasty Plot and clean. This is Calvin's playground illusion team: the first apparent Mew is a local Zorua, the second is real, and Smeargle plus Jigglypuff make the deception function as a complete four-Pokémon plan. No later encounter will reuse this false-ace structure.
entries.behavior: Calvin uses normal foe-aware doubles scoring plus partner support, speed-control preference, and smart switching. No move or turn is forced; the sets are deliberately legible to the general AI.
entries.counterplay: This team has several answers rather than one key. Spread attacks expose Illusion and bypass Follow Me, Taunt shuts down Jigglypuff or Smeargle, priority finishes a Sash-broken Smeargle, and early Bug, Ghost, and Dark options pressure Mew. The player can also double-target the support slot, contest speed with their own Icy Wind or Electroweb, or overwhelm the frail Zorua lead.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Mew plus sand is sound, but Hippopotas/Drilbur/Fairy support is a familiar reusable weather module and does not fit Calvin's playful trickster identity as well as Illusion does.

full_team_candidates.decision: individual set selected
full_team_candidates.reason: The full generated team has no Route 102 identity, but its Zorua is an exact fit for the false-Mew lead.

full_team_candidates.decision: individual set selected
full_team_candidates.reason: The full team is unrelated to the route, while its Nasty Plot Mew is the correct protected ace for this composition.

full_team_candidates.decision: support shell selected
full_team_candidates.reason: The full team is not imported; Smeargle's redirection shell is adapted specifically to enable Calvin's Mew.

corpusReview.decision: No full random or sample team is copied verbatim. Three sourced sets are integrated into one route-specific Illusion plan, with Jigglypuff supplying the missing speed and partner support.

competitiveReferences.adaptation: Zorua's Expert Belt, Illusion, Hidden Power Fighting, Dark Pulse, Extrasensory, and Sucker Punch set is imported verbatim as the deceptive lead.
Smeargle keeps the donor's Fake Out, Helping Hand, and Follow Me support shell; Focus Sash plus Endeavor replaces King's Shield so it cannot become a harmless final slot.
Mew's Sitrus Berry, Psyshock, Nasty Plot, Aura Sphere, and Will-O-Wisp set is imported as the real late-game ace.
The bulky Jigglypuff support donor is rebuilt for active doubles tempo with Friend Guard, Icy Wind, Helping Hand, Dazzling Gleam, and Protect.

entries.closure: Battle 2 is the first full-team doubles exam. It is difficult because the player must identify the false Mew, manage active speed and partner support, and preserve an answer for a level-15 Nasty Plot Mew—not because the battle demands one preselected counter.

entries.uniquenessExplanation: Closest unrelated roster: Amy & Liv (14% species overlap). Its species appear across an average of 1.5 unrelated trainer families.

entries.name: Rick
entries.plan: Focus Sash Water Bubble Dewpider establishes Sticky Web while threatening real special coverage. Choice Band Anorith immediately punishes the Fire and Flying attacks invited by the Bug theme, Eviolite No Guard Karrablast is the only setup threat, and level-16 Life Orb Larvesta closes through recoil-limited physical pressure and U-turn rather than a mature Quiver Dance sweep. This is Verdant's juvenile Bug Web lesson: all four species are first-stage, Anorith and Karrablast appear on no other current trainer, Dewpider appears only in mutually exclusive later rival branches, and Larvesta's other uses are substantially later. The mature Leavanny/Scizor/Heracross/Frosmoth version is preserved for a cap-55 Bug specialist.
entries.behavior: Rick remains an intentional singles pacing fight. First-turn setup preference makes Sticky Web or Karrablast's Swords Dance worth considering, while smart switching and normal foe-aware scoring preserve attacks, Choice locking, recovery, and pivots. No move or opening is forced.
entries.counterplay: Taunt, multihit attacks, or immediate pressure can deny Web; Flying and Levitate Pokémon ignore it, and legal removal clears it. Wingull, Shinx, Blitzle, Rotom, Bonsly, Rock coverage, priority, and faster Choice users are already available. Intimidate, burns, and physical walls constrain the three backliners, while Water and Rock pressure force Larvesta to spend recoil or recovery turns. No one counter is required.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Galvantula supplies an attacking Sticky Web lead model, but the surrounding Altaria, Poliwrath, Sceptile, Dusknoir, and Persian form an unrelated mature singles team.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Armaldo provides the correct Rock-and-Bug retaliation shell, but the complete doubles team does not fit a young Route 102 Bug Catcher and the evolved fossil itself belongs later.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Escavalier's Megahorn and Swords Dance role is ideal inspiration, but its five partners and mature final form do not belong in the cap-14 chapter.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Life Orb Volcarona demonstrates late Fire/Bug pressure, but Quiver Dance and the final form are deliberately replaced by a recoil-limited juvenile Larvesta pivot.

corpusReview.decision: All 983 teams were reviewed, and none contains any exact proposed four-species overlap because competitive corpora rarely use these first stages. Rick therefore adapts four mature competitive roles to stage-legal youngsters instead of pretending a verbatim tournament team belongs at cap 14.

competitiveReferences.adaptation: Dewpider translates Galvantula's attacking Web lead into a legal juvenile: Focus Sash preserves one action, while Water Bubble Scald plus Ice Beam and Giga Drain prevent the lead from becoming dead weight.

Anorith inherits Armaldo's X-Scissor and Rock Slide coverage; Choice Band, Aqua Jet, and Knock Off make the unevolved fossil an immediate anti-Fire and anti-Flying breaker rather than another setup slot.
Karrablast receives Escavalier's Megahorn and Swords Dance identity. Eviolite and No Guard support legal Drill Run and Knock Off, leaving it as the team's single setup win condition.

The mature Volcarona donor is not copied. Larvesta keeps only its Life Orb Fire/Bug pressure and uses legal Flare Blitz, U-turn, Wild Charge, and Morning Sun so recoil and imperfect coverage keep the level-16 ace answerable.

entries.closure: Battle 3 is 10/10 because it proves unevolved Pokémon can support a real competitive hazard plan. Web feeds three distinct physical tempos, but the team has one Sash, one setup slot, exploitable shared weaknesses, recoil, a Choice lock, and several independent forms of counterplay.

entries.name: Allen
entries.theme: Fake Out tempo + active speed control + priority pressure
entries.plan: Light Ball Lightning Rod Pikachu and Toxic Orb Guts Taillow lead with Fake Out, Electroweb speed control, priority, immediate damage, and protection from Electric targeting. Eviolite Dry Skin Paras and Sitrus Quick Feet Zigzagoon form the back-line setup mode: Rage Powder or Spore can buy Belly Drum, then Extreme Speed supplies pressure. Allen weaponizes three true first-stage Pokémon and one young mascot through real doubles roles: Light Ball Pikachu, Guts Taillow, Eviolite redirection Paras, and Belly Drum Zigzagoon. Leading with offense keeps the later Rage Powder setup from repeating Calvin's opening redirection pattern. Wally's current Mauville redirection-plus-Belly Drum module is explicitly flagged for replacement when that encounter is audited.
entries.behavior: Allen uses normal foe-aware doubles scoring plus partner awareness and contextual speed control. The AI can choose immediate Pikachu and Taillow pressure before the later redirection option appears; Rage Powder, Spore, Belly Drum, Fake Out, Electroweb, Protect, and attacks are evaluated normally, with no forced move, target, turn, or switch.
entries.counterplay: The opening pair is vulnerable to Ground, Rock, Intimidate, and coordinated targeting; Protect can also expose Fake Out or consume Taillow's first Guts turn. When the back line appears, Fake Out, Taunt, spread damage, early Grass or Overcoat Pokémon, Hatenna's Magic Bounce, Fire or Flying pressure, or a double target can remove the frail Eviolite Paras before it buys a free Drum. Dreepy, Rotom, and other Ghosts ignore Extreme Speed and Facade, while Intimidate and burns hinder Zigzagoon. The player can disrupt either wave without predicting a forced opening.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Its Belly Drum Zigzagoon is ideal, but Gardevoir, Kabutops, Quagsire, Regice, and Leafeon form an unrelated six-Pokémon collage with no early-route identity or redirection plan.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Parasect's redirection role fits, but its mature form and the surrounding Blacephalon, Mega Banette, Slurpuff, Seviper, and Toucannon belong later. Only the legal support role is adapted to young Paras.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: The complete rain, Shell Smash, Web, and Mega Metagross team has no early-route identity. Its Light Ball Pikachu utility set remains fully compatible.

full_team_candidates.decision: rejected as a full import
full_team_candidates.reason: Taillow appears beside Zapdos, Spiritomb, Luxray, Snubbull, and Cacturne in the wrong battle format. Only its exact Guts cleaner set fits Allen.

corpusReview.decision: No complete team contains more than one of these four Pokémon. Four competitive roles are integrated into one 'beginner Pokémon, expert doubles' battle with three first-stage members, one young mascot exception, one setup move, and no guaranteed redirection Sash.

competitiveReferences.adaptation: Zigzagoon keeps Quick Feet, Belly Drum, Extreme Speed, and Seed Bomb; Sitrus Berry plus Protect replaces Leftovers plus Substitute so the doubles setup is powerful but interactable.

Parasect's Dry Skin, Spore, Protect, Seed Bomb, and Rage Powder shell is moved down to level-15 Paras. Eviolite replaces Sitrus Berry so the first-stage supporter remains useful without pretending it already evolved at level 24.

Pikachu keeps Light Ball, Lightning Rod, Fake Out, Encore, and Volt Tackle. Electroweb adds foe-only spread speed control, while Encore gives the fragile lead an active punish instead of another generic Protect.
Taillow's Toxic Orb, Guts, Protect, Quick Attack, Brave Bird, and Facade set is imported verbatim as the level-15 closer.

entries.closure: Battle 4 is difficult because either two-Pokémon wave can snowball, but neither begins behind guaranteed redirection and every enabling action has several legal interruptions. It now demonstrates the intended progression rule directly: young Pokémon can execute expert doubles without being replaced by premature evolved forms.

entries.name: Tiana
entries.plan: Focus Sash Snow Warning Amaura and Eviolite Slush Rush Alolan Sandshrew lead with Aurora Veil, accurate Blizzard, fast Ice and Steel pressure, and Brick Break utility. Choice Band Thick Fat Swinub adds Ice Shard priority, Rock Slide spread damage, and Superpower, while level-16 Expert Belt Slush Rush Arctozolt is the single-stage Bolt Beak ace. This is Verdant's first full weather battle and its juvenile fossil snow lesson. Amaura and Alolan Sandshrew appear on no other current trainer, Swinub's only other use is a much later level-one gimmick, and no Battles 1-4 species repeats. The mature Ninetales-A/Froslass/Mamoswine shell is preserved for cap-70 Route 133 trainer Linda.
entries.behavior: Tiana uses foe-aware smart switching plus field-control and first-turn setup preferences. Snow is automatic; Aurora Veil receives a contextual bonus without being forced, and the now-irrelevant generic speed-control profile is removed because no team member uses an active speed-control move.
entries.counterplay: Remove or replace snow, Taunt or double-target Sash Amaura before Veil, break Veil, or use Wide Guard against Blizzard and Rock Slide. Fire, Fighting, Rock, Steel, Ground, and Water coverage hit different members; Flying and Levitate avoid Ground coverage, priority and Trick Room bypass Slush Rush, and Intimidate or burns contain all three physical attackers. Protect punishes Bolt Beak timing, and the team has no second setup mode once Veil is denied.

full_team_candidates.decision: juvenile lead role selected, full team rejected
full_team_candidates.reason: Focus Sash Snow Warning Aurorus supplies the correct Aurora Veil, Blizzard, and Earth Power shell, but the mature final form and its five partners belong later. Amaura carries the role legally at cap 14.

full_team_candidates.decision: juvenile physical role selected, full team rejected
full_team_candidates.reason: Alolan Sandslash supplies the Slush Rush Steel-and-Ice pressure model, but its final form and unrelated team are replaced by Eviolite Alolan Sandshrew without Swords Dance.

full_team_candidates.decision: juvenile set selected, full team rejected
full_team_candidates.reason: The corpus actually contains a competitive Swinub, but Bayleef, Machoke, Jolteon, Staravia, and Gliscor do not form Tiana's snow squad.

full_team_candidates.decision: fossil speed role selected, full team rejected
full_team_candidates.reason: Slush Rush Arctozolt is the right single-stage payoff, but Alolan Ninetales and the mature OU shell are tabled for a later snow specialist.

corpusReview.decision: No complete youthful snow team fits verbatim. Four mature competitive roles are translated into three first-stage Pokémon and one single-stage fossil, with one setup axis and no premature final evolution.

competitiveReferences.adaptation: Amaura inherits Aurorus's Focus Sash, Snow Warning, Aurora Veil, Blizzard, and Earth Power shell. Protect replaces Stealth Rock for a fragile doubles lead.

Alolan Sandshrew keeps Sandslash's Slush Rush and Iron Head identity. Eviolite, Icicle Crash, Brick Break, and Rapid Spin create immediate juvenile pressure and an active answer to the player's field setup without importing Swords Dance.
Swinub's corpus set already supplies Icicle Crash and Superpower. Choice Band, Ice Shard, and Rock Slide turn it into a no-setup priority and spread attacker.
Arctozolt keeps the mature team's Slush Rush Bolt Beak identity; Expert Belt, Icicle Crash, Stomping Tantrum, and Protect make the true single-stage fossil the legal level-16 ace.

entries.closure: Battle 5 is 10/10 because three young Pokémon and one true fossil create a complete snow puzzle without premature evolutions. Weather, Veil, two distinct Slush Rush attackers, priority, spread damage, and Bolt Beak make it severe, while every dependency has several independent answers.

entries.name: Billy
entries.plan: Choice Scarf Imposter Ditto turns the player's chosen lead into the opening puzzle and explains Billy's strange tracks. Focus Sash Wimpod can Taunt or place one Spike before Wimp Out creates natural tempo; Eviolite Water Compaction Sandygast supplies recovery and status; level-16 Solid Rock Tirtouga is a reactive Weakness Policy ace with dual STAB, priority, and item removal rather than another setup move. Billy's footprint dialogue now describes a literal young shoreline mystery: a copied set of tracks, a fleeing beach bug, a living sand pile, and a fossil turtle from the cliffs. None appears in Battles 1-5; Sandygast and Tirtouga appear on no other current trainer, and Wimpod appears only once much later. The mature haunted shoreline quartet is preserved for a later ocean or abandoned-ship encounter.
entries.behavior: Billy remains a deliberate singles pacing fight. Imposter and Wimp Out function automatically; normal foe-aware scoring understands the Choice lock, hazards, recovery, status, Weakness Policy, and priority, while smart switching escapes bad copies or matchups. The obsolete Tailwind speed-control profile is removed, and no move or turn is forced.
entries.counterplay: Lead with a low-impact or status-focused Pokémon, exploit Ditto's Choice lock, or remove its Scarf. Taunt, multihit attacks, status, or immediate pressure limit Wimpod's one action. Special Water, Grass, Ice, Ghost, Dark, and Knock Off pressure Sandygast. Burn, Intimidate, Encore, item removal, safe neutral damage, or one decisive Grass attack avoids or answers Tirtouga's Weakness Policy. Ditto's variable type, Sandygast's Electric immunity, and Wimpod's Grass neutrality prevent one attack from solving the full sequence.

entries.name: Darian
entries.plan: Level-17 Choice Scarf Remoraid and Expert Belt Dazzling Bruxish form the first cast: full-HP Water Spout attacks immediately while Dazzling blocks priority and Bruxish applies Taunt, screen breaking, and physical coverage. Sitrus Intimidate Qwilfish and level-16 Focus Sash Clamperl form the second cast: Thunder Wave and Intimidate buy one Shell Smash opportunity, then Muddy Water or Ice Beam converts it into pressure. Darian becomes Verdant's two-cast young-fish puzzle. Remoraid appears once, Bruxish twice, Qwilfish eight times, and Clamperl zero times across all 983 references; none appears in Battles 1-6. The mature OCIC quartet remains preserved for a later tournament-style opponent instead of being lost.
entries.behavior: Native doubles scoring understands Water Spout's HP scaling, Choice locking, Dazzling, Intimidate, Shell Smash, Muddy Water, Protect, and Thunder Wave. Darian adds HP awareness, smart switching, first-turn setup preference, and contextual speed control. Neither wave is scripted: Remoraid can change its Choice lock, Bruxish can attack or Taunt, and Clamperl's Smash remains interruptible.
entries.counterplay: Any normal-speed hit weakens Water Spout; Storm Drain, Water Absorb, Dry Skin, Water resistance, Protect, Wide Guard where legal, or removing Remoraid's Scarf punish the first cast. Dazzling blocks priority but not ordinary attacks. Taunt, a double target, special pressure, Haze, Clear Smog, Trick Room, or phazing stops or reverses Clamperl; Grass and Electric attacks remain strong, while Qwilfish's Poison coverage and Clamperl's Ice Beam stop one-button sweeping. No exact capture or turn sequence is required.

entries.name: Cindy
entries.theme: Fake Out tempo + Trick Room + pivot control
entries.plan: Eviolite Buneary scouts with Fake Out and Encore, then Focus Sash Competitive Gothita conditionally reverses speed. Level-17 Brave Huge Power Mawile spends the finite Trick Room turns attacking immediately; fast Choice Band Debutante Furfrou is intentionally awkward inside Trick Room and becomes the closer after it expires. Cindy's luxury pets look polished, but the sequence has a real temporal seam. This is Verdant's first Trick Room lesson and its first deliberate doubles-to-singles pacing release. None of the four species appears in Battles 1-7, Debutante Furfrou gives the Lady class a native visual signature, and the fast last slot makes Trick Room a limited resource rather than a reusable module.
entries.behavior: Cindy remains a native singles trainer. Foe awareness and smart switching understand immunities, U-turn, Choice lock, and bad matchups; contextual speed control uses Trick Room only when reversing order helps the current board. Setup-first-turn is deliberately absent because Gothita may enter later, and no trainer-specific forced turn is required.
entries.counterplay: Ghosts blank most of Buneary, while Taunt, multihit attacks, item removal, or reversing Trick Room stop Gothita. Fire, Ground, burn, Intimidate, Protect, and physical walls contain Mawile; Fighting pressures both Normal types, but Gothita punishes it and Mawile is neutral. Special damage ignores Fur Coat, and Furfrou's Choice lock can be exploited. The player can win through offense, denial, bulk, status, or speed-order manipulation rather than one required catch.

entries.name: Winston
entries.plan: Focus Sash Power Spot Stonjourner and Eviolite Download Porygon are Winston's expensive display pieces: Power Spot passively multiplies Porygon's damage, Download may add another offensive boost, Rock Slide applies spread pressure, and Wide Guard reacts to revealed spread moves. Sitrus Cheek Pouch Dedenne uses Super Fang and Nuzzle to create a finite opening for Air Balloon Honedge's one interruptible Swords Dance and priority endgame. Winston is the first Power Spot battle and the only early fight framed as an expensive rare collection. None of the four species appears in Battles 1-11, and its passive damage aura, Super Fang chip, Wide Guard reaction, Balloon seam, and delayed setup do not repeat prior weather, Web, Trick Room, detonation, theft, or Perish modules. Winston2-4 remain separate five-badge rematch indices and must later preserve these families through legal Porygon and Honedge growth rather than reverting to the old Bidoof and Pidgey roster.
entries.behavior: Normal foe-aware scoring includes the partner Power Spot multiplier in damage calculation. Smart switching handles Porygon's matchup and Honedge's setup position; contextual speed control values Nuzzle. Download, Cheek Pouch, No Guard, Super Fang, Wide Guard, Protect, priority, and Choice-free attacks use native behavior. Setup-first-turn is deliberately absent because Honedge enters later, and no move is forced.
entries.counterplay: Special attacks or focused damage remove Sash Stonjourner and its Power Spot, while Knock Off strips Porygon's Eviolite. Fighting pressures Porygon but Stonjourner and Honedge change that matchup. Ground threatens Dedenne but initially misses Balloon Honedge; Fire, Dark, Ghost, burn, Taunt, Intimidate, Haze, Clear Smog, Protect, and priority all contain Honedge. Wide Guard reacts only to known spread pressure, and popping the Balloon is visible counterplay. No one team slot is mandatory.

entries.name: Haley
entries.plan: Every slot embodies Haley's choice theme. Eviolite Eevee opens with the Yawn decision while remaining active through Adaptability, Extreme Speed, and Bite. Focus Sash Trace Ralts can Encore a passive response but has no Disable lock. Choice Specs Snorunt visibly commits to one of four special coverage lines. Life Orb Hunger Switch Morpeko changes Aura Wheel between Electric and Dark every turn and can reconsider with Parting Shot. Haley is the only early branching-evolution and changing-mind battle. None of the four families appears in Battles 1-12, and the fight uses no weather, hazard, trapping, detonation, Perish timer, item theft, or free stat setup. Haley2-4 remain separate cap-55 rematch indices: they must show Vaporeon/Gardevoir/Glalie, then Jolteon/Gallade/Froslass, then Sylveon plus both Ralts and Snorunt branches, rather than the current unrelated Arceus roster.
entries.behavior: Haley remains a native singles trainer. Smart switching handles Snorunt's Choice lock, type immunities, and Parting Shot; first-turn setup preference makes Yawn plausible without forcing it; HP-aware scoring improves Protect and endgame decisions. Hunger Switch and Aura Wheel type changes are native. No trainer-only move, target, or turn script is added.
entries.counterplay: Taunt, sleep immunity, Safeguard, Electric Terrain, U-turn, or ordinary switching answer Yawn. Fighting pressures Eevee and Morpeko; Steel, Poison, Dark, and priority break Ralts; Fire, Rock, Fighting, and Steel plus Choice-lock exploitation check Snorunt. Ground blocks Electric Aura Wheel but not its alternating Dark turn or Seed Bomb, while Fairy, Bug, burn, Intimidate, and Protect contain Morpeko. No one wall or required catch solves all four.

entries.name: Gina & Mia
entries.theme: Dancer physical relay + Dancer recital + Dancer special relay
entries.plan: Flying Gem Dancer Oricorio and Eviolite Mold Breaker Axew open the recital. Axew's Dragon Dance also raises Oricorio's Attack and Speed, turning the gem-powered Acrobatics into a physical reveal; Oricorio can instead use Revelation Dance, Roost, or Protect. Focus Sash Sweet Veil Cutiefly then brings Quiver Dance, which Dancer copies into special pressure, while Black Sludge Oddish's Petal Dance makes Oricorio repeat an immediate Grass attack. Every reserve has independent STAB and protection, so breaking the centerpiece weakens the choreography without reducing three partners to dead props. This is Verdant's only three-dance recital and the first fight whose apparent boss changes attacking category according to the partner beside it. Oricorio, Axew, Cutiefly, and Oddish do not appear in Battles 1-13. The team uses no weather, Web, Fake Out, redirection, active speed-control move, Trick Room, detonation, screen, theft, Perish timer, Power Spot, Super Fang, or Yawn module. The flower-lined Route 104 setting and two overworld twins make the synchronized choreography feel native rather than assigned globally.
entries.behavior: Gina and Mia use normal foe-aware doubles scoring, smart switching, first-turn setup awareness, and the reusable combo profile. That profile gives a contextual bonus to any FLAG_DANCE move while a living Dancer partner is present; it does not force a move, target, turn, or switch. Dancer itself, Flying Gem consumption, Sweet Veil, Black Sludge, Protect, Roost, Petal Dance lock, and every stat change remain native engine behavior.
entries.counterplay: Oricorio has a visible 4x Rock weakness and is also vulnerable to Electric, Water, and focused neutral damage; removing it ends every copied dance. Taunt, Encore, Haze, Clear Smog, phazing, Trick Room, Unaware, priority, or doubling the current dancer stops a snowball. Steel and Poison pressure Cutiefly, Ice and Fairy pressure Axew, and Fire, Flying, Ice, or Psychic pressure Oddish. Intimidate and burn blunt the Dragon Dance/Acrobatics line, while special walls blunt the Quiver/Petal line. The player may attack the centerpiece, deny the initiator, reverse speed, or outlast finite items—no exact catch or turn sequence is required.

entries.name: Ivan
entries.theme: Sash Endeavor lure + Schooling HP threshold + Water pressure
entries.plan: Ivan is a single-battle pacing break built as lure, sinker, hook, and school. Focus Sash Luvdisc invites an apparent easy knockout, then trades HP with Endeavor or releases into a counter through Flip Turn. Stunfisk is immune to the obvious Electric answer and can punish contact with Static while attacking both defenses and using Pain Split. Eviolite Tentacool resists the obvious Grass answer and returns Poison, Ice, Water, or Grass coverage. Level-20 Assault Vest Wishiwashi finally forms its 620-BST School, but loses that form as soon as it falls to one-quarter HP. This is Verdant's only fishing-cast singles sequence and first Schooling threshold puzzle. Luvdisc, Stunfisk, Tentacool, and Wishiwashi do not appear in Battles 1-14. It deliberately follows a doubles recital with a talk-only single and uses no rain, speed-control move, setup, hazard, trap, Perish timer, screen, redirection, detonation, item theft, dance, Choice lock, or repeated Water Spout/Shell Smash module. Dondozo and Tatsugiri remain available for a later native Commander double.
entries.behavior: Ivan remains a native singles trainer with universal foe awareness, viability and faint checks, smart switching, and HP-aware scoring. Existing damage estimation understands Endeavor's current-HP damage, discourages it while Luvdisc has more HP, and values it below half HP; native switching can catch an Electric attack with Stunfisk or a Grass attack with Tentacool. Schooling's level-20 and one-quarter-HP transitions are native. No trainer-only move, target, switch, or turn script is added.
entries.counterplay: Priority, Ghost immunity, Taunt, multihit attacks, or preserving a low-HP target answer the Sash-Endeavor lure. Water, Grass, Ice, strong special damage, noncontact attacks, and recovery answer Stunfisk; Ground, Psychic, Electric, and strong physical damage answer Tentacool despite Eviolite. Wishiwashi can be burned, intimidated, walled on either attacking side, hit with fixed damage or priority, or deliberately pushed below its visible one-quarter Schooling threshold. Smart switching means one Electric or Grass move is useful but never an automatic sweep; no exact catch, starter, or turn sequence is required.

corpusReview.decision: All 983 competitive references and three independent concept families were reviewed. The one complete team containing two chosen species supplies the central bait; three exact role donors are then adapted by hand into a four-catch fishing sequence with no imported weather, hazard, setup, trapping, Perish, screen, or repeated early-game module.

competitiveReferences.adaptation: Focus Sash Soul-Heart Luvdisc keeps Surf, Endeavor, and Flip Turn. Ice Beam replaces Substitute so the Sash survives until Endeavor matters; the checked-in legal Gen 9 donor also restores Endeavor to Luvdisc's tutor compatibility.
Leftovers Static Stunfisk keeps Discharge, Earth Power, and Scald from the exact donor. Pain Split replaces Stealth Rock so the sinker is a live HP exchange rather than another entry-hazard lesson.
Eviolite Liquid Ooze Tentacool combines the donors' Sludge Bomb, Scald, Ice Beam, and coverage-tank identity. Legal Giga Drain keeps it active while punishing neither side with another status lock.

Assault Vest Schooling Wishiwashi retains Earthquake, Ice Beam, and mixed offense. Liquidation provides reliable physical Water STAB and U-turn lets smart AI reset an unfavorable catch when a reserve remains.

entries.closure: Battle 15 is 10/10 because every member embodies a different part of Ivan's fishing metaphor and every obvious counter is useful without sweeping the roster. Three stage-valid catches at levels 16-17 establish the bait, then a level-20 Schooling ace creates a severe but transparent HP-threshold finish. Four perfect spreads, distinct items, modern-legal moves, adaptive singles AI, and broad type, tempo, contact, status, priority, and threshold counterplay make it an 8.9/10 optional puzzle.

entries.name: Lyle
entries.plan: Normal Gem Sturdy Pineco and Light Clay Telepathy Dottler lead. Dottler chooses a relevant screen while Pineco chips or waits until damage makes Explosion worthwhile; Telepathy makes the blast safe. Removing Dottler first destroys that safe window. Eviolite Sturdy Dwebble then supplies Rock spread pressure and item denial, while Life Orb Compound Eyes Joltik attacks specially with accurate Thunder so Intimidate or one physical wall cannot solve the fight. Lyle is Verdant's safe-detonation lesson and the first battle centered on Telepathy rather than a generic weather, Web, Fake Out, redirection, Trick Room, or stat-setup module. Three exact species have zero representatives in the 983-team corpus, none appears in Battles 1-8, and the sole evolved member is the visually young, legally level-10 Dottler.
entries.behavior: Native ally-damage scoring recognizes Telepathy's Explosion immunity. Lyle adds smart switching, field-control scoring for the relevant screen, HP awareness that discourages a full-health blast, and WILL_SUICIDE so a damaged Pineco can actually take the safe opportunity. Removing Dottler changes that decision naturally; no turn, target, or move is forced.
entries.counterplay: Ghost leads, Protect, Wide Guard, Damp, burn, multihit attacks through Sturdy, Fake Out, or focusing Dottler can absorb or prevent the blast. Taunt, Brick Break, Psychic Fangs, Defog, or mixed damage answer the screens. Water, Grass, and Steel pressure Dwebble; Ground immunity stops Thunder but Energy Ball punishes many Ground and Rock answers. Fire remains broadly strong, Knock Off removes every durability item, and priority limits Joltik. No single catch or precise turn sequence is required.

corpusReview.decision: All 983 references were reviewed. No complete team contains two of these four families. Exact Pineco, Dottler, and Joltik appear zero times and Dwebble once, so four individually proven roles are combined into a unique young-Bug encounter instead of forcing a mature full-team import.

competitiveReferences.adaptation: Pineco inherits Forretress's Sturdy, Gyro Ball, and Protect shell. Normal Gem Explosion and Bug Bite are legal Pineco-native additions that create the encounter's one high-risk payoff.
Dottler inherits Orbeetle's Struggle Bug, Psychic, and Light Screen; Light Clay Reflect replaces repeated Sticky Web, and its legal Telepathy slot supplies the interactive safe-blast partner.
Dwebble keeps the donor's Sturdy and X-Scissor identity. Eviolite, Rock Slide, Knock Off, and Protect replace Shell Smash so the battle does not repeat Darian's setup module.

Joltik legally de-evolves Galvantula's Life Orb Compound Eyes Thunder and Bug Buzz shell. Energy Ball punishes Ground and Rock answers, while Volt Switch gives the reserve an active escape instead of another generic Protect.

entries.closure: Battle 9 is 10/10 because a visible partner ability turns Explosion from raw power into an interruptible board puzzle: attack Pineco, remove Dottler, defend against the blast, or exploit its timing. The second pair covers physical-only answers without duplicating the gimmick. Levels 15-17, optimized items, and one severe payoff make it 8.4/10 while leaving many independent solutions.

entries.name: Grunt
entries.plan: Focus Sash Prankster Purrloin and Eviolite Adaptability Skrelp open the smash-and-grab: Fake Tears amplifies special pressure, Thunder Wave and Icy Wind contest speed, Encore punishes passive turns, and Knock Off starts the robbery theme. Choice Band Adaptability Corphish brings priority and immediate commitment; Life Orb Contrary Inkay is the sole snowball, raising Attack and Defense only while using Superpower. This is the one early smash-and-grab battle: three Knock Off users are intentional because the Grunt is literally stealing papers and valuables. None of the four species appears in Battles 1-9, the team uses no weather, Web, redirection, Fake Out, Trick Room, safe Explosion, or free setup move, and the story dialogue already fits a coordinated multi-Pokémon ambush.
entries.behavior: Foe-aware smart switching handles immunities and Choice lock. Contextual speed control scores Thunder Wave and Icy Wind, while the first-turn setup preference makes Purrloin consider Fake Tears or Encore without forcing either. Contrary Superpower, Adaptability, priority, Protect, and Knock Off use native scoring; no battle script dictates a move or target.
entries.counterplay: Early Dark types ignore Prankster-targeted status; Taunt or focused damage removes Purrloin, while Electric, Grass, Ground, and Psychic coverage pressure the aquatic or Poison members. Fairy, Bug, and Fighting attacks check the thieves; burn, Intimidate, Haze, Clear Smog, Unaware, Protect, and priority limit Inkay. Corphish's Choice lock is exploitable, and no one attack hits all four cleanly. The fight supports broad team-building rather than a single required capture.

entries.name: James
entries.theme: Bug pressure + Perish trap + residual control
entries.plan: Sitrus Celebi and Eviolite Shelmet form the forest circle: Perish Song starts a shared timer, Infestation traps only one target, Encore punishes stalling, Struggle Bug reduces incoming special pressure, and Protect buys finite turns. Removing either lead breaks the complete plan. Focus Sash Nincada uses Toxic, Dig, and Protect as the escape pair's countdown piece; Choice Scarf Moxie Heracross supplies immediate closing pressure without setup. James is Verdant's first Perish-trap lesson and a deliberate early mythical sighting. Celebi appears as a forest spirit rather than random raw BST, Shelmet and Nincada preserve the dialogue's later growth promise, and exact species do not repeat Battles 1-10. The current James2-4 records remain separate future encounter indices; at their five-badge cap-55 unlock they must visibly evolve Nincada and Shelmet, preserve Celebi and Heracross, and use consistent native battle formats rather than being silently treated as part of this closure.
entries.behavior: James uses the existing reusable Perish-trap profile plus smart switching. It values Perish Song only with a trapping partner, favors Infestation on a perishing target, uses Protect while the count is safe, avoids redundant or suicidal songs, and exits at count one when a bench exists. The profile strongly encourages the concept but never forces a turn; Celebi can attack, Shelmet can Encore or use Struggle Bug, and the player can disrupt the board.
entries.counterplay: Taunt or focused damage can stop Celebi before the song or remove Shelmet before Infestation. Soundproof blocks Perish Song, Ghost types escape trapping, the untrapped slot can switch normally, and ordinary switching resets a Pokémon's own count. Celebi has seven exploitable weaknesses; Fire, Flying, and Rock pressure Shelmet and Heracross; Water, Ice, Fire, and Flying pressure Nincada. Knock Off removes the Eviolite, Protect cannot stop Perish Song itself, and eliminating either half of the lead dismantles the puzzle. No exact capture is required.

entries.name: Josh
entries.plan: Mental Herb Sturdy Shuckle and Sitrus Sheer Force Cranidos open the Gym's geology lab. Guard Split averages Shuckle's enormous defenses with Cranidos's frailty, turning the fossil breaker into a temporary tank while making Shuckle much easier to remove; Helping Hand and Rock Tomb keep the donor useful. Eviolite Storm Drain Lileep catches the obvious Water attack and can convert it into Giga Drain, Ancient Power, or Earth Power pressure while Stockpile creates a separate denial target. Focus Sash Toxic Debris Glimmet supplies fast special Rock and Poison pressure, can use Rock Polish, and punishes careless physical damage with Toxic Spikes. This is Verdant's only defense-transfer geology lab and the first Rustboro Gym lesson. Shuckle, Cranidos, Lileep, and Glimmet do not appear in Battles 1-15. It uses no weather, Trick Room, Tailwind, Fake Out, redirection, dance, detonation, Perish timer, active trap, screen, item theft, Choice lock, friendly damage, Weakness Policy, Schooling, or prior Water Spout, Shell Smash, Power Spot, or Guard Split module. Toxic Spikes arise reactively from Toxic Debris rather than from another scripted hazard lead.
entries.behavior: Josh uses native doubles guards, foe and partner awareness, smart switching, first-turn setup, combo, and speed-control profiles. Guard Split scoring now recognizes a partner target only while Shuckle's combined defenses exceed that partner's; the combo profile gives that useful transfer a moderate bonus, and the condition becomes false after the stats equalize so it is not repeated. Rock Tomb, Helping Hand, Stockpile, Rock Polish, Storm Drain, Sturdy, Sheer Force, Toxic Debris, Sash, Eviolite, and Sitrus behavior remain native. No move, target, turn, or switch is forced.
entries.counterplay: Immediate focus fire, Encore, Disable, phazing, or a second Taunt after the one-use Mental Herb can stop Guard Split; after it resolves, Shuckle has surrendered much of its own bulk. Burn, Intimidate, Fighting, Ground, Grass, Steel, Water, speed control, Wide Guard, or attacking Cranidos before the transfer answer the breaker. Storm Drain blocks lazy Water targeting but not Grass, Fighting, Ice, Bug, or Steel pressure on Lileep. Special attacks avoid Toxic Debris; priority, multihit attacks, Ground, Psychic, Steel, or focused damage remove Sash Glimmet. The player may deny the donor, race the recipient, exploit the weakened donor, route around Water, or manage the triggered hazard—there is no required catch or move order.

Eviolite Sturdy Nosepass adds Wide Guard and Thunder Wave. Expert Belt Tough Claws Binacle closes with single-target Water, Fighting, Rock, and Ghost coverage rather than another setup or Rock Slide module. This is Verdant's only repeat-after-me battle and its only early team whose main threat depends on preserving action order between a teacher and pupil. Oranguru, Tyrunt, Nosepass, and Binacle do not appear in Battles 1-16. It uses no weather, terrain, Trick Room, Tailwind, Fake Out, redirection, dance, detonation, Perish timer, trap, screen, item theft, Choice lock, friendly damage, defense transfer, Toxic Debris, Schooling, or prior Water Spout, Shell Smash, Power Spot, or Guard Split module.
entries.behavior: Tommy uses the native doubles guard, foe and partner awareness, smart switching, combo, and speed-control profiles. Existing partner scoring already permits Instruct when the chosen partner move is spread; the combo profile now adds a contextual bonus only when a living partner has actually selected a both-foes or foes-and-ally move. It does not force Instruct, Rock Slide, a target, a turn, or a switch. Wide Guard, Strong Jaw, Tough Claws, Sturdy, Life Orb, Eviolite, Sitrus, Thunder Wave, and Protect remain native.
entries.counterplay: Taunt, Disable, Encore, Imprison, sleep, paralysis, speed reversal, or removing either half stops Instruct; Dark, Bug, and Ghost pressure Oranguru, while Fighting, Ground, Ice, Steel, Dragon, and Fairy pressure Tyrunt. Wide Guard, Protect, Rock resistance, Intimidate, burn, screens, or ordinary focus fire contain the repeated Rock Slide without requiring a single species. Fighting, Ground, Grass, Steel, and Water pressure Nosepass, while Electric, Grass, Ground, Fighting, and strong neutral damage answer Binacle. The player may break the teacher, break the pupil, reverse their action order, guard the spread move, or out-position the reserves.

entries.plan: Rocky Helmet Sturdy Shieldon opens the strata by establishing Stealth Rock on global turn zero, while Metal Burst, Rock Tomb, and Iron Head punish a careless hit. Choice Scarf Unaware Woobat then Tricks a move lock onto the player or pivots with U-turn while retaining Psychic and Air Slash. Eviolite Cursed Body Galarian Corsola can disable that locked move, lower Attack and heal with Strength Sap, burn into Hex, or erase boosts with Haze, making a switch through the rocks attractive but costly. Level-17 Life Orb Unnerve Aerodactyl closes with fast Rock, Ground, Flying multihit, and Water coverage. This is Verdant's only shifting-strata singles battle and first authored sequence in which a Choice lock can collide with Cursed Body across an entry hazard. Shieldon, Woobat, Galarian Corsola, and Aerodactyl do not appear in Battles 1-17. It uses no weather, terrain, Trick Room, Tailwind, Instruct, Guard Split, dance, detonation, Perish timer, active trap, screen, redirection, friendly damage, Weakness Policy, Schooling, or repeated early setup sweeper; Stealth Rock is a deterministic layer supporting a switch puzzle rather than another generic hazard lead.
entries.behavior: Marc remains a native singles trainer with smart switching, first-turn setup, and HP-aware profiles. Setup scoring makes lead Shieldon's Stealth Rock plausible only on global turn zero; native Trick logic values exchanging a Choice Scarf and rejects Sticky Hold or otherwise invalid targets. Native HP and viability checks understand Strength Sap, Will-O-Wisp, Hex, Haze, Metal Burst, U-turn, Cursed Body, Sturdy, Rocky Helmet, Eviolite, and Life Orb. entries.counterplay: Taunt, Magic Bounce, multihit attacks, Mold Breaker, status, hazard removal, or attacking without contact limit Shieldon's Sturdy setup and Rocky Helmet. Knock Off, Sticky Hold, an itemless target, Protect scouting, Dark or Electric pressure, or accepting and exploiting the known Choice lock answer Woobat. Taunt, Knock Off, special Dark or Ghost attacks, Toxic, Heal Block, or strong special focus break Corsola; Haze also prevents it from rewarding a setup-only plan. Water, Electric, Ice, Rock, Steel, priority, burn, Intimidate, or preserving a fast revenge killer answer Aerodactyl. No one move or catch solves all four layers.

entries.name: Roxanne
entries.plan: Mental Herb Prankster Klefki and Eviolite Vital Spirit Rockruff open the protected confidence exam. Klefki can establish Safeguard before most disruption, then Swagger a physical ally for +2 Attack without confusion; Foul Play and Protect prevent a passive support lock. Rockruff supplies fast Rock Slide, Psychic Fangs, Sucker Punch, and Protect. Sitrus Own Tempo Mudbray can accept Swagger even when Safeguard is denied, while High Horsepower and Heavy Slam diversify pressure. Life Orb Rock Head Bonsly turns Double-Edge into recoil-free force, Assault Vest Water Absorb Maractus blocks single-target Water autopilot, and level-19 Expert Belt Clear Body Regirock closes with four aggressive coverage attacks and no Protect. This is Verdant's only protected-confidence examination and the only opening boss with six entirely stage-valid young or single-stage Pokémon. Klefki, Rockruff, Mudbray, Bonsly, Maractus, and Regirock do not appear in Battles 1-18. It uses no weather, terrain, Trick Room, Tailwind, Instruct, Guard Split, hazard, trap, Perish timer, dance, detonation, redirection, friendly damage, Weakness Policy, Schooling, or Mega. The lone legendary appears as an aggressive mineral ace rather than a stack of unrelated boss legends.

Confusion eligibility includes side Safeguard; beneficial partner Swagger is exempt from the generic bad-confusion penalty when Safeguard protects a physical recipient, and the combo profile moderately favors Safeguard before Swagger and Swagger only beside Safeguard or Own Tempo. Those conditions do not force a move, target, turn, or switch. Prankster, Mental Herb, Foul Play, Own Tempo, Rock Head, Water Absorb, Clear Body, Sucker Punch, Rock Slide, Protect, and every held item remain native.
entries.counterplay: Focus fire, Fake Out into Rockruff, Dark-type Prankster immunity, Encore, Imprison, or a second Taunt after Mental Herb can break Klefki's sequence. Haze, Clear Smog, Unaware, Psych Up, Spectral Thief, Reflect, Charm, Intimidate, Wide Guard, Protect, phazing, item removal, or stalling Safeguard all answer boosted Rock Slide without prescribing one species. Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, Steel, Ice, Psychic, Flying, Bug, Poison, priority, and special pressure divide naturally across Rockruff, Mudbray, Bonsly, and Maractus. Regirock has five common weaknesses, no recovery, and no Protect; Clear Body blocks Intimidate, but burn's damage penalty, ordinary status damage, and special type pressure still work. No one catch or move order solves the six.

entries.name: Jerry
entries.plan: The joint branch now opens with the circuit it advertised: Terrain Extender Pincurchin uses Discharge beside level-24 Choice Band Motor Drive Klink, accelerating its immediate Gear Grind, Wild Charge, Return, or Rock Smash pressure without harming it. Janice's Life Orb Mimikyu attacks immediately behind Disguise, leaving Sitrus Unburden Swirlix as the composition's one setup clock. Jerry follows Klink with Fake Out and Encore Togedemaru, then Ground-covering Elekid. Each split half still has immediate damage, disruption, and a closer. This is Verdant's first Electric Terrain practical and its only native pair whose opening deliberately attacks its own immune partner. The former three parallel setup clocks are reduced to one later Swirlix clock. Pincurchin, Mimikyu, Swirlix, Togedemaru, Elekid, and Klink do not appear in Battles 1-25, and the fight repeats no weather, Gravity, Wonder Room, Trick Room, hazard, Anger Point, Battery, or Mega module.
entries.behavior: Both trainers remain single-format three-member records for native pairing. entries.counterplay: Overwrite terrain, use Ground, Lightning Rod, Volt Absorb, Wide Guard, burn, Intimidate, or focused damage into the visible Pincurchin-Klink lead. Break Disguise and Sturdy with chip or multihit attacks; remove Air Balloon, Sitrus, Life Orb, Choice Band, or Terrain Extender; exploit Klink's move lock; and reserve Taunt, Encore, Haze, or phazing for Swirlix's single Belly Drum clock. Scald, Ice Punch, Fairy, Fighting, Steel, Poison, Ground, and Fire coverage keep one immunity from solving every slot.

entries.name: Grunt
entries.theme: Water pressure + residual control + spread + Wide Guard
entries.plan: Leftovers Unaware Dondozo swallows Focus Sash Commander Stretchy Tatsugiri and opens at +2 in Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def, and Speed. Only Dondozo acts while the commander is hidden, and Order Up can compound Speed; if Dondozo falls, Tatsugiri reappears with Muddy Water, Dragon Pulse, Taunt, and Protect. Black Sludge Corrosion Salandit then poisons even nominal Poison or Steel answers, while Eviolite Merciless Mareanie converts poison into critical Venoshock pressure and supplies Wide Guard, Recover, and Haze. Both waves are one Aqua hierarchy and escape-cover story. This is Emerald Champions' first canonical Commander battle and the intentional payoff for a core reserved twice earlier. Dondozo, Tatsugiri, Salandit, and Mareanie do not appear in Battles 1-26. It uses no prior weather, terrain, room, Gravity, hazard, Anger Point, Battery, or Mega module.
entries.behavior: The Grunt uses a guarded double, partner awareness, and combo scoring but deliberately no smart switching so the authored Commander lead is not dismantled. Canonical Commander removes Tatsugiri's action and switching, grants Dondozo five +2 boosts, and stores Stretchy form so Order Up can raise Speed even if the swallowed Tatsugiri later faints. Combo scoring also rewards Toxic only beside Merciless or Venoshock against a legal target. No target or turn is forced.
entries.counterplay: Haze and Clear Smog erase all five Commander boosts; Grass, Electric, Water immunity, burn, Intimidate, Reflect, recoil exploitation, and concentrated damage contain the one acting Dondozo. Tatsugiri cannot be targeted or forced out while swallowed, but dropping Dondozo exposes it. Safeguard, Misty Terrain, Lum Berry, status immunity, Taunt, Knock Off, Ground, Psychic, Electric, or removing Salandit before Toxic stops the poison wave. Nothing requires one catch or precise turn script.

entries.name: Ned
entries.plan: Focus Sash Dazzling Finneon leads beside Life Orb Swift Swim Arrokuda. Finneon can establish rain without priority interruption, then Scald, Ice Beam, or U-turn; Arrokuda immediately threatens Liquidation, Close Combat, Psychic Fangs, or Protect. Eviolite Thick Fat Spheal follows with Freeze-Dry, Brine, Encore, and Protect so opposing Water answers are not free. Sitrus Gulp Missile Cramorant finishes through Surf-triggered form pressure, rain-accurate Hurricane, Ice Beam, and Roost. The battle is one readable fishing tide, not a scripted state machine. This is Verdant's first Dazzling-protected rain sprint and first Gulp Missile showcase. Finneon, Arrokuda, Spheal, and Cramorant do not appear in Battles 1-28. It deliberately revisits visible weather immediately after the rival, but changes the question from a dynamic starter forecast to a short physical rain race with a form-based closer and no Tailwind, Icy Wind, terrain, room, setup, trap, hazard, or Mega.
entries.behavior: Ned uses native partner-aware, HP-aware, and field-control scoring only. Party order guarantees the Finneon-Arrokuda lead; existing weather logic values Rain Dance beside Water pressure, while Dazzling, Swift Swim, Freeze-Dry, Encore, Protect, Gulp Missile, Hurricane accuracy, recoil, and recovery execute natively. No custom selector, target, or forced turn is required.
entries.counterplay: Taunt, focus fire, weather replacement, Cloud Nine, Air Lock, Electric or Grass pressure, Wide Guard, screens, bulky Water resistance, item removal, and speed reversal all remain broad answers. Finneon has only one Focus Sash and rain is finite; Arrokuda takes Life Orb recoil; Spheal is slow; and Cramorant must use Surf before Gulp Missile matters. Denying rain weakens the whole team without making it helpless.

entries.plan: Eviolite Water Absorb Frillish opens with Whirlpool, Night Shade, Recover, and Taunt, creating a finite undertow the player can break rather than an endless stall loop. Choice Specs Mega Launcher Clauncher then commits to Water Pulse, Dragon Pulse, Ice Beam, or Sludge Bomb and can be punished through the revealed lock. This is Verdant's first three-depth singles sequence and first Choice Specs Mega Launcher plus White Herb Skill Link progression. Frillish, Clauncher, and Shellder do not appear in Battles 1-29. It immediately releases the player from two consecutive doubles, uses no weather, active speed-control move, priority move, Protect, terrain, room, partner activation, Mega, or custom AI, and revisits Shell Smash only after more than twenty encounters in a different format.
entries.behavior: Elliot remains an intentional single and uses only native smart-switching and HP-aware scoring. Whirlpool, Night Shade, Recover, Taunt, Choice lock, Mega Launcher, White Herb, Shell Smash, and Skill Link are existing mechanics; no custom move order, forced setup turn, or trainer-specific selector is added. Match Call registration and later rematch routing remain untouched.
entries.counterplay: Taunt, Ghost or Dark pressure, trapping escape, fixed-damage races, item removal, and strong Grass or Electric damage answer Frillish. Scout and exploit Clauncher's Choice lock with immunities, resistances, Protect, or switching. Priority, status, Haze, Clear Smog, phazing, Unaware, Focus Sash, multihit resistance, or denying the setup turn answer Shellder. No one counter is required to solve all three depths.

entries.plan: Sitrus Volt Absorb Pachirisu and Lum Defiant Falinks lead. Eviolite Synchronize Kirlia creates the special lane through Dazzling Gleam, Psychic, Will-O-Wisp, and Helping Hand. Toxic Orb Poison Heal Breloom attacks immediately through Facade, Mach Punch, Seed Bomb, and Rock Tomb. Level-25 Mega Hawlucha is the sole ace: No Guard makes High Jump Kick and Stone Edge reliable while also making the player's inaccurate answers reliable against it; Brave Bird and Feint complete the direct finish. This is Verdant's first opposing Mega, definitive early redirection-and-commitment boss, and only reciprocal No Guard Hawlucha puzzle. Pachirisu, Falinks, Hitmontop, Kirlia, Breloom, and Hawlucha do not appear in Battles 1-35. Wide Guard can be baited with single-target damage; item removal attacks Eject Button, Eviolite, Lum, Sitrus, Toxic Orb, and Hawluchanite seams. Flying, Psychic, Fairy, Electric, Ice, and Rock pressure Mega Hawlucha, and No Guard reciprocally makes inaccurate player moves hit it. The boss has no Protect anywhere, so coordinated offense is always meaningful.

It deliberately keeps Carkol and Sandygast unevolved at cap 30 and turns Johanna's line about hot battles making Pokémon tougher into two literal ally-activation routes. Sandygast last appeared thirty-eight encounters earlier in Billy's simple shoreline single; its Eviolite Water Compaction reserve job is a deliberate, materially different reuse. entries.name: Grunt
entries.theme: Water pressure + active speed control + residual control
entries.plan: Figy Gluttony Alolan Raticate and Black Sludge Liquid Ooze Tentacruel open the heist. Super Fang removes half of current HP without creating a hidden knockout, while Knock Off, Sucker Punch, and Taunt punish passive recovery; Tentacruel may Toxic one resource, lower special defense with Acid Spray, control speed with Icy Wind, or attack through Hydro Pump. Choice Band Adaptability Basculin converts damaged targets through Aqua Jet, Waterfall, Crunch, or Psychic Fangs. Expert Belt Rock Head Relicanth closes as the stolen exhibit with Head Smash, Waterfall, Body Press, or Protect. HP, status, and PP persist into Battle 47; player held items do not. This is Verdant's first explicitly cross-battle attrition opener and first Alolan Raticate, Tentacruel, Basculin, and Relicanth exact-species use. The Aqua thief, chemical controller, direct fish, and ancient exhibit form a museum heist without rain, Tailwind, ally activation, terrain, room, screen, hazard, setup, redirection, trapping, Mega, or Primal. Its primary question is not merely winning, but choosing how much HP, status, and PP can safely carry into the immediate cleanup battle.
entries.behavior: Grunt 1 uses no-intro doubles with native foe-aware, smart-switching, partner-aware, HP-aware, and speed-control scoring. Super Fang, Gluttony, Figy Berry, Liquid Ooze, Toxic, Acid Spray, Icy Wind, Choice Band, Adaptability, priority, Rock Head, and Expert Belt are existing mechanics. No custom selector, forced target, field engine, setup flag, Mega, or Primal is added. The entry script requires two usable Pokémon once; a one-survivor 1-v-2 continuation into Grunt 2 is intentionally supported by the native absent-battler path.
entries.counterplay: Ghost typing blocks Super Fang outright, while immediate Fighting, Fairy, Bug, strong special offense, Taunt, Substitute, recovery, Protect cycling, or removing Raticate before a second action also limits the HP tax. Steel and Poison typing, Immunity, Poison Heal, Magic Guard, Safeguard, Misty Terrain, Substitute, Heal Bell, Aromatherapy, Natural Cure, or focused Ground, Psychic, or Electric pressure limit Tentacruel and persistent Toxic. Water resistance or immunity, burn, Intimidate, Protect, priority denial, item removal, and exploiting Basculin's Choice lock answer the conversion. Grass, Electric, Ground, Fighting, special Water, or denying Head Smash accuracy pressure Relicanth. The player may prioritize winning cleanly over taking every knockout quickly because Battle 47 starts immediately.

entries.plan: The natural joint branch leads Throat Spray Serene Grace Meloetta beside Leftovers Regenerator Audino. Every loaded joint member—Meloetta, Wigglytuff, Chatot, Audino, Slurpuff, and Frogadier—can use Round: when one singer follows another in the same turn, it acts immediately and doubles its Round power. Wigglytuff adds Competitive Fairy/Ice coverage, Chatot adds Focus Sash Chatter and Heat Wave, Audino adds Heal Pulse and Helping Hand, Sitrus Unburden Slurpuff adds Fairy/Fire pressure, and Expert Belt Protean Frogadier changes type through Round, Water Pulse, Ice Beam, or Dark Pulse. In split Isabel, Meloetta plus Wigglytuff remain an attacking duet and Eviolite Regenerator Gossifleur is the fourth support. In split Kaleb, Audino plus Slurpuff remain a support/offense duet and Rocky Helmet Regenerator Eldegoss is the fourth support. Neither split-only member is required by the joint six. This is Verdant's first Round chorus, first Meloetta encounter, and first exact Wigglytuff, Chatot, Gossifleur, Audino, Slurpuff, and Eldegoss opponent use. Frogadier deliberately repeats twenty-one encounters after appearing as one possible dynamic rival middle stage; here it is an Expert Belt Protean sound/coverage reserve in a completely different native-pair branch. entries.name: Kaleb
entries.plan: The natural joint branch leads Throat Spray Serene Grace Meloetta beside Leftovers Regenerator Audino. Every loaded joint member—Meloetta, Wigglytuff, Chatot, Audino, Slurpuff, and Frogadier—can use Round: when one singer follows another in the same turn, it acts immediately and doubles its Round power. Wigglytuff adds Competitive Fairy/Ice coverage, Chatot adds Focus Sash Chatter and Heat Wave, Audino adds Heal Pulse and Helping Hand, Sitrus Unburden Slurpuff adds Fairy/Fire pressure, and Expert Belt Protean Frogadier changes type through Round, Water Pulse, Ice Beam, or Dark Pulse. In split Isabel, Meloetta plus Wigglytuff remain an attacking duet and Eviolite Regenerator Gossifleur is the fourth support. In split Kaleb, Audino plus Slurpuff remain a support/offense duet and Rocky Helmet Regenerator Eldegoss is the fourth support. Neither split-only member is required by the joint six. This is Verdant's first Round chorus, first Meloetta encounter, and first exact Wigglytuff, Chatot, Gossifleur, Audino, Slurpuff, and Eldegoss opponent use. Frogadier deliberately repeats twenty-one encounters after appearing as one possible dynamic rival middle stage; here it is an Expert Belt Protean sound/coverage reserve in a completely different native-pair branch. The design follows four mandatory doubles with a lighter playful question and no rain, Primal, Mega, Tailwind, cross-battle attrition, ally activation, status clock, hazard, screen, setup move, trap, redirection, or custom selector.
entries.behavior: Both trainers retain the ordinary single-script geometry required for native pairing and use foe-aware, smart-switching, partner-aware, HP-aware, and combo-setup scoring. The reusable combo layer now rewards Round when the active partner knows or has chosen Round; it never fixes a target or forces both moves. Throat Spray, Competitive, Chatter, Regenerator, Heal Pulse, Helping Hand, Unburden, Protean, Eviolite, Rocky Helmet, and all coverage are existing mechanics. No trainer-specific state machine, weather, Tailwind, room, terrain, Mega, or Primal is added.
entries.counterplay: Ghost typing and Soundproof block the Normal-type Round users; Steel and Poison pressure the Fairy singers; Rock, Electric, and Ice pressure Chatot; Bug, Dark, and Ghost pressure Meloetta; physical focus fire exploits the mostly special roster. Taunt, Heal Block, Encore, item removal, priority, spread attacks, Snarl, Light Screen, special walls, Trick Room, paralysis, and denying the first singer break or reverse the chorus. Protean Frogadier can change weaknesses but has no Protect or Focus Sash, and both split-only Grass supports are passive enough to focus. Round coordination increases tempo and power but does not create trapping, redirection, immunity to ordinary damage, or a forced target.

entries.name: Timmy
entries.plan: Level-31 Focus Sash Run Away Roaming Gimmighoul opens with Shadow Ball, Hidden Power Fighting, Thief, or Protect; once its Sash breaks, Thief can exploit the empty item slot. Level-32 Eviolite Aftermath Stunky uses Foul Play, Sucker Punch, Sludge Bomb, and Flamethrower as a mixed physical-punishment and contact check. Level-32 Shuca Lightning Rod Plusle attacks through Thunderbolt, Grass Knot, or Dazzling Gleam and can Encore a passive turn. Level-33 Life Orb Dry Skin Heliolisk closes through Thunderbolt, spread Hyper Voice, Glare, or Protect. Every exact species is a current Route 110 grass encounter. There is no team-wide weather, room, screen, setup move, Mega, or Primal. This is the first closed Heliolisk opponent appearance, alongside the first closed Roaming Gimmighoul, Stunky, and Plusle appearances, and the first exact-catch ecological sampler. Heliolisk's Dry Skin, high Speed, focused Electric pressure, and spread Normal pressure make the source-last ace distinct without borrowing Rotom from its New Mauville generator event. The low-cohesion single is a deliberate palate cleanser after cutters, Arena Trap, and false-focus redirection, not a failed doubles module.
entries.behavior: Timmy uses native foe-aware, smart-switching, and HP-aware singles scoring. Focus Sash, Run Away, Hidden Power Fighting, Thief, Protect, Eviolite, Aftermath, Foul Play, Sucker Punch, Shuca Berry, Lightning Rod, Encore, Life Orb, Dry Skin, Thunderbolt, Hyper Voice, and Glare are existing mechanics. No partner flag, forced move, custom selector, speed flag, setup flag, Mega, or Primal is added.
entries.counterplay: Dark or Ghost pressure answers Gimmighoul; Ground after Shuca pressures Plusle, Stunky, and Heliolisk while Hyper Voice prevents one immunity from blanking the ace. Physical attacks exploit Plusle and Heliolisk, item removal strips every safety item, and Taunt limits Encore and Glare. Stunky's Sucker Punch can be played around, Foul Play discourages careless physical setup, and Aftermath punishes contact without preventing noncontact damage; Gimmighoul's post-Sash Thief is weak enough to manage without hidden randomness.

Level-33 Assault Vest Stalwart Duraludon closes through Flash Cannon, Dragon Pulse, Thunderbolt, or Body Press. The team uses one finite speed move and no weather, terrain, room, trap, redirection, setup move other than ally Decorate, Mega, or Primal. The 21 middle starters deliberately recur from the earlier Rustboro rival as continuity, now twenty-six encounters later and only one-sixth of a substantially deeper team. May and Brendan have exact gameplay parity; no gender branch is secretly easier.

entries.counterplay: Fake Out, Taunt, priority, opposing speed control, Trick Room, or direct pressure can stop Type: Null's timing; Water Absorb, Storm Drain, Dry Skin, Protect, burn, Intimidate, Choice-lock exploitation, or faster offense answer Dracovish. entries.name: Edwin
entries.plan: The joint branch leads level-31 White Herb Justified Terrakion beside level-31 Wide Lens Houndoom. Houndoom can Beat Up Terrakion, while Heat Wave, Snarl, and Will-O-Wisp remain independent options. Edwin's split instead leads Terrakion beside level-31 Occa Prankster Cottonee with Beat Up, Helping Hand, Charm, and Giga Drain; level-32 Flying Gem Archen and level-33 Expert Belt Eelektrik then attack directly. Joseph's split leads Houndoom beside level-31 Eviolite Justified Growlithe with Flare Blitz, Close Combat, Crunch, and Morning Sun; level-29 Berry Juice Rattled Toxel provides Nuzzle, Endeavor, Metal Sound, and Tearful Look before level-33 Soft Sand Moxie Krokorok closes through Dig, Crunch, Rock Slide, and Ice Fang. No weather, terrain, room, screen, Tailwind, setup move, Mega, or Primal is used. This is the first closed Terrakion, Cottonee, Archen, Eelektrik, Houndoom, Growlithe, Toxel, and Krokorok opponent appearance and Verdant's definitive Beat Up plus Justified showcase. Unlike the recent every-member Round circuit, only the branch's opening pair owns the activation; the loaded reserves change axis immediately. The older Frost Breath, Guard Split, and Surf activation lessons use different recipients, costs, and counterplay.
entries.behavior: Both trainers use native foe-aware, smart-switching, partner-aware, HP-aware, and combo-setup doubles scoring. The existing combo profile adds a strong bonus only when Beat Up targets a live Justified partner; ordinary ally-safety scoring rejects lethal activation. White Herb, Prankster support, Flying Gem Acrobatics, Defeatist, Levitate, Rattled, Endeavor, Moxie, Dig, and all coverage are existing mechanics. No forced opener, custom target selector, speed profile, field profile, Mega, or Primal is added.
entries.counterplay: Fake Out, Taunt, Follow Me or Rage Powder, priority, immediate Houndoom or Cottonee focus fire, Protect on the intended recipient, Ghost interaction where applicable, burn, Intimidate after activation, Haze, Clear Smog, Unaware, phazing, or a fast recipient knockout all answer the headline. Rock, Ground, Water, Fighting, Fairy, Ice, and special pressure cover Terrakion or Growlithe by phase. Archen exposes Defeatist, Toxel is deliberately under the cap, Eelektrik has modest raw stats, and Krokorok's Dig telegraphs a turn. No single answer solves every reserve, but none requires a lock-and-key counter.

entries.name: Edward
entries.plan: Level-31 itemless Levitate Lunatone sets Magic Room and attacks or heals. Edward's level-32 Hypno, level-32 Magic Bounce Xatu, and split-only level-33 Munna remain itemless and use direct Psychic coverage, Disable, Future Sight, U-turn, and recovery. Alyssa leads level-31 itemless Immunity Gligar; in her split, level-32 Competitive Gothorita supplies Magic Room. Level-32 Aftermath Drifblim and split-only level-33 Motor Drive Emolga exploit itemless Acrobatics and pivoting. Player held-item effects are suppressed for five turns, but abilities, moves, and stats remain intact. No Protect, priority, active speed control, setup move, weather, terrain, Gravity, Mega, or Primal is used. This is the first closed Lunatone, Hypno, Xatu, Munna, Gligar, Gothorita, Drifblim, and Emolga opponent appearance and Verdant's first Magic Room equipment-denial lesson. The rejected Gravity draft was discarded because Battle 23 already owns the native-pair Gravity/Hustle architecture. Magic Room instead turns Verdant's unusually generous held-item access into one transparent counter-puzzle.
entries.behavior: Edward and Alyssa use foe-aware, smart-switching, HP-aware, and field-control scoring. Native Magic Room scoring already rewards the move when the user and partner are itemless while the opposing side holds items, prevents duplicate casting, and rejects recasting while active. Native Future Sight scoring rewards one pending delayed attack and suppresses duplicates. No custom selector, forced opener, combo profile, speed profile, Mega, or Primal is added.
entries.counterplay: Taunt, Encore, immediate Lunatone or Gothorita focus fire, Magic Room reversal, or simply surviving five turns restores items. Dark, Ghost, and Bug pressure Edward; Ice, Water, Rock, and strong neutral attacks pressure Alyssa by slot. Abilities, raw stats, recovery, hazards, status, screens, weather, terrain, and item-independent move combinations continue functioning. Future Sight is visible and can be timed; U-turn and Volt Switch can be punished with hazards or trapping.

entries.name: Dale
entries.plan: Level-31 Sitrus Storm Drain Lumineon uses Soak, Scald, Air Slash, or Protect beside level-32 Expert Belt Water Absorb Arctovish with Freeze-Dry, Fishious Rend, Crunch, and Rock Slide. Level-32 Scope Lens Sniper Octillery can exploit Soak with Energy Ball before Focus Energy raises its critical pressure through Hydro Pump or Ice Beam. Level-33 Mystic Water Water Veil Floatzel closes through Waterfall, Aqua Jet, Ice Punch, or Crunch. No rain, speed field, trap, redirection, ally activation, Mega, or Primal is used. This is the first closed Lumineon, Arctovish, Octillery, and Floatzel opponent appearance and Verdant's first Soak target-painting lesson. Friendly Surf activation was rejected because Battles 38 and 44 already own related ally-Water conversion shapes.
entries.behavior: Dale uses foe-aware, smart-switching, partner-aware, HP-aware, and combo-setup doubles scoring. The reusable combo layer now rewards Soak when the partner owns Electric, Grass, or Freeze-Dry conversion and rewards the corresponding exploiting move when the partner selected Soak; it never fixes a target. Native logic rejects already-Water targets. Focus Energy, Sniper, Storm Drain, Water Absorb, and all coverage are existing mechanics.
entries.counterplay: Fake Out, Taunt, Encore, redirection, Substitute, Magic Bounce, immediate Lumineon focus fire, or Water-type targets deny Soak value. Lightning Rod, Volt Absorb, Grass resistance, special bulk, Snarl, Light Screen, burn, Intimidate, Wide Guard against Rock Slide, Haze or immediate Octillery pressure, and priority into Floatzel remain broad answers.

entries.name: Anthony
entries.plan: Level-30 Sharp Beak Tangled Feet Doduo uses Brave Bird, Double-Edge, Jump Kick, and Steel Wing. Level-31 Magnet Sap Sipper Zebstrika uses Wild Charge, Overheat, Double-Edge, and Low Kick. Level-32 Sitrus Sheer Force Rampardos uses Head Smash, Superpower, Zen Headbutt, and Iron Head. Level-33 Wise Glasses Download Porygon-Z uses Hyper Beam, Tri Attack, Ice Beam, and Dark Pulse. Every member attacks immediately; there is no setup, Protect, priority, pivot, field, weather, trap, Choice lock, Mega, or teammate dependency. This is the first closed Doduo, Zebstrika, Rampardos, and Porygon-Z appearance and the first zero-setup no-brakes commitment ladder. It deliberately follows Jaclyn's staged setup single with pure immediate damage, mixed axes, and mandatory drawbacks rather than another enabler-recipient or field engine.
entries.behavior: Anthony retains an ordinary singles trainer battle with foe-aware viability and smart switching. Native recoil safety, crash behavior, damage and KO scoring, stat-drop handling, Download, berries, and Hyper Beam recharge execute the design. The AI is not forced to save Hyper Beam for a KO; an imperfect raw-damage commitment is an intentional player opening, not a hidden script. No custom selector is added.
entries.counterplay: Protect, Ghost or type immunities, resistance pivots, recovery, recoil management, and forcing Jump Kick misses create immediate punish windows. Burn, Intimidate, Reflect, bulky Ground, Rock, Steel, or physical walls answer the first three; special bulk, Fighting pressure, Disable, Encore, or exploiting recharge answers Porygon-Z. The player can win through survival and timing instead of outracing every leg.

This is the first closed Gastrodon, Scolipede, Ponyta, and Snorlax appearance and the first literal swim-cycle-run-recovery endurance race. entries.name: Wattson
entries.theme: Electric pressure + Fake Out tempo + Tailwind
entries.plan: Level-32 Terrain Extender Electric Surge Tapu Koko uses Wild Charge, Nature's Madness, U-turn, and Taunt. Level-32 Focus Sash Lightning Rod Emolga uses Tailwind, Encore, Helping Hand, and Thunderbolt; Koko may safely feed Lightning Rod with Wild Charge, but Emolga's Flying typing means Electric Terrain does not boost its attack. Level-33 Assault Vest Quark Drive Iron Hands uses Fake Out, Close Combat, Wild Charge, and Ice Punch. Level-33 Sitrus Armor Tail Farigiraf uses Twin Beam, Icy Wind, Light Screen, and Protect. Level-34 Eviolite Download Porygon2 uses Trick Room, Tri Attack, Ice Beam, and Recover. Level-35 Raichunite Y Raichu Mega Evolves into No Guard and uses Thunder, Focus Blast, Grass Knot, and Protect. Four of six members are Electric-type; Farigiraf and Porygon2 are the two essential off-type control modules. There is no redirection, weather, second terrain, trap, Primal, Tera, Z-Move, Dynamax, or second Mega. Tapu Koko, Iron Hands, Farigiraf, Porygon2, and Raichu are new to the 67 closed encounters. Emolga returns twelve battles after B56's optional split-only Magic Room reserve as Wattson's fixed Lightning Rod Tailwind lead; the type identity and role earn the reuse. Story-correct Battle 48 no longer spends Raichu, so Wattson now owns its first reveal and level-35 No Guard Mega payoff. B67 explicitly replaced Farigiraf with Simisage to protect this priority-denial reveal. Four Electric-types make the Gym identity dominant without discarding two essential control roles.
entries.behavior: Wattson uses foe-aware, smart-switching, partner-helping, HP-aware, field-control, speed-control, and combo scoring. Terrain and Quark Drive are automatic; Porygon2 is the only Trick Room setter. A reusable speed guard strongly penalizes Tailwind, Icy Wind, Electroweb, and paralysis while stable Trick Room has more than one turn left, prevents inactive Trick Room and fast control from being selected together, and discourages Trick Room when the active partner already outruns both visible foes. Partner scoring now returns no chosen move when the ally is switching or using an item, so stale move positions cannot create a false combo. On every knockout, pivot, or voluntary switch, native replacement logic chooses by predicted resistance and outgoing damage rather than source order. Once Raichu is active, existing Mega-aware move evaluation scores it as No Guard Mega Y before accuracy and move decisions; native trainer logic then forces Mega Evolution on its first legal move action, not on a fixed encounter turn. No field, speed mode, target, replacement, or ordinary move is forced.
entries.counterplay: Ground spread pressure, Lightning Rod, Volt Absorb, Motor Drive, Grass resistance, terrain replacement, and stalling attack the current field; removing Terrain Extender only prevents a later Koko entry from refreshing it for eight turns. Taunt, Encore, Imprison, opposing Trick Room, competing Tailwind, paralysis, Icy Wind, Protect cycling, and focus fire attack move order. Remove Farigiraf before relying on priority. Burn, Intimidate, Ground, Psychic, Fairy, and physical walls answer Iron Hands; Knock Off, Trick, Taunt, Encore, Fighting damage, or opposing Trick Room answer Porygon2; Ground, strong physical priority after Farigiraf, or normally inaccurate high-power attacks answer No Guard Mega Raichu. The player can preserve one reciprocal Mega for whenever Raichu enters.

competitiveReferences.adaptation: Terrain, Iron Hands, Farigiraf, priority denial, and two speed circuits are preserved without Tera or restricted Miraidon; Whimsicott's support role is translated to Electric-native Emolga.
Porygon2 retains Eviolite, Trick Room, Ice Beam, and Recover as the sole slow-mode setter.
Tapu Koko retains Taunt and pivot pressure while Terrain Extender makes field duration a player decision.
Raichu occupies the last source slot as No Guard Mega Y, replacing donor X and gaining live-legal accurate Thunder/Focus Blast coverage; native replacement scoring may deploy it earlier.

Emolga keeps the donor's Helping Hand support, adds legal Tailwind and Encore, and converts an optional allied Lightning Rod boost through Thunderbolt as Wattson's fourth Electric-type. Its Flying typing correctly prevents Electric Terrain from boosting that move.

authorSelfCheck.strongest_part: The fixed opening teaches the vocabulary, then every adaptive reserve pairing asks the player to reclassify the board without abandoning the Terrain, priority, and speed identity.

The partner-move conflict guard prevents Wattson's two mixed-speed pairs from establishing opposite controls on the same turn; Mega Raichu from +5 to +4 is the first runtime tuning knob.
